extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the SINGULAR computer-algebra system; computational algebraists needing library procedures for divisors, Groebner bases over function fields, and finite-difference schemes
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (divisors.lib, ffmodstd.lib, finitediff.lib), giving usage, assumptions, returns, theory and examples for each routine used in algebraic geometry, modular Groebner computations, sparse interpolation, and finite-difference scheme construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: negativedivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: negativedivisor(A); A = divisor. Assume A is a divisor on X. Return: a divisor on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: The procedure interchanges numerator and denominator ideals (A*(-1) effect). Example shows makeDivisor and then negativedivisor producing swapped numerator/denominator. Usage note: input must be a divisor object on the scheme/qring X.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalForm
rubrics_metrics.description: normalForm(A); A = divisor. Assume A is a divisor on X. Return: different representative of the same divisor on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Cancels common components of numerator and denominator. Example: constructing D from added divisors then normalForm(D) returns simplified representative. Use to canonicalize divisor representation before comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: isEqualDivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: isEqualDivisor(A,B); A = divisor, B = divisor. Assume A and B are divisors on X. Return: int 0 or 1, checks equality of A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Computes normal forms of A and B and compares them. Example: isEqualDivisor(A,D) returns 1 when D normalizes to A. Use after normalizing or when equality check needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: globalSections
rubrics_metrics.description: globalSections(A); A = divisor. Assume A is a divisor on X. Return: a list with a basis of the space of global sections of D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Assumes qring of X satisfies S2-condition and X is smooth. Computes sat((f*J) : I)/f where D = (I)-(J). Example shows basis elements returned. Use for computing section spaces H^0(X,O(D)).

rubrics_metrics.name: degreeDivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: degreeDivisor(A); A = divisor. Assume A is a divisor on X. Return: The degree of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Computes difference of the degrees of numerator and denominator ideals. Example: degreeDivisor(P) returns integer degree. Useful for numerical invariants of divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: linearlyEquivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: linearlyEquivalent(A,B); A = divisor, B = divisor. Assume A and B are divisors on X. Return: list if A and B are linearly equivalent and int 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Checks whether A-B is principal. If yes, returns list L=(f,g) where A-B = (f/g). Example: returns 0 or a 2-list of functions. Use to detect linear equivalence and obtain explicit principal divisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: effective
rubrics_metrics.description: effective(A); A = divisor. Assume A is a divisor on X which is linearly equivalent to an effective divisor. Return: divisor on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Computes an effective divisor linearly equivalent to A. Example: effective(D) returns an effective representative. Use when need an effective representative of a linear equivalence class.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeFormalDivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: makeFormalDivisor(L); L = list. Assume L is a list of tuples of an integer and a divisor. Return: a formal divisor on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Represents an integer formal sum of divisors. Example shows creating -5*A + 2*B. Use to build formal combinations before evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: evaluateFormalDivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: evaluateFormalDivisor(D); D = formal divisor. Assume D is a formal divisor on X. Return: a divisor on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Evaluates the formal integer sum into a single divisor. Example: evaluateFormalDivisor(makeFormalDivisor(...)) returns combined divisor. Use to convert formal sums to concrete divisor objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: formaldivisorplus
rubrics_metrics.description: formaldivisorplus(A,B); A = formaldivisor, B = formaldivisor. Assume A and B are formal divisors on X. Return: a formal divisor on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Adds the integer formal sums element-wise. Example demonstrates adding two formaldivisors and outputting summed components. Use to combine formal sums before evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: negativeformaldivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: negativeformaldivisor(A); A = formaldivisor. Assume A is a formaldivisor on X. Return: a formal divisor on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Changes the signs of the coefficients of the formal divisor. Example shows sign inversion. Use to negate formal sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: multformaldivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: multformaldivisor(n,A); n = integer, A = formaldivisor. Assume n is an integer and A is a formal divisor on X. Return: a formal divisor on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Multiplies the formal sum by integer n. Example: fE*2 doubles coefficients. Use for scalar multiplication of formal divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: degreeFormalDivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: degreeFormalDivisor(A); A = formaldivisor. Assume A is a formaldivisor on X. Return: The degree of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Computes degrees of the summands and returns the weighted sum according to coefficients. Example returns integer (possibly negative). Use to compute degree of an integer linear combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: makePDivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: makePDivisor(L); L = list. Assume L is a list of tuples of an integral polyhedron and a divisor such that all polyhedra have the same tail cone. Return: a pdivisor on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Represents a polyhedral formal sum of divisors (a p-divisor). Example shows building pdivisor with polytopes and divisors, output indicates tail cone and summands. Use when working with T-varieties or polyhedral divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: evaluatePDivisor
rubrics_metrics.description: evaluatePDivisor(D,v); D = pdivisor, v = intvec. Assume D is a polyhedral divisor on X and v is a point in the dual of the tailcone of the coefficients. Return: a formal divisor on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Evaluates the polyhedral sum at v to obtain an integer formal sum (pdivisor -> formaldivisor). Example shows integer coefficients multiplied into divisors. Requires v in correct dual cone.

rubrics_metrics.name: pdivisorplus
rubrics_metrics.description: pdivisorplus(A,B); A = pdivisor, B = pdivisor. Assume A and B are polyhedral divisors on X. Return: a pdivisor on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: Adds polyhedral formal sums by performing Minkowski sums of polyhedral coefficients. Example shows resulting pdivisor retains tail and summands. Use to combine polyhedral divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: ffmodstd/lib overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of ffmodstd.lib: library for computing Groebner bases of ideals in polynomial rings over algebraic function fields Q(T) using modular methods and sparse multivariate rational interpolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory/approach: map ideal via T -> T*z and evaluate at many integer points b to compute Groebner bases mod primes, reconstruct coefficients via sparse multivariate rational interpolation (uses univariate interpolation, rational reconstruction, Berlekamp/Massey, etc.). References and algorithmic ingredients listed. Use when needing Groebner bases over Q(T) with high probability reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: fareypoly
rubrics_metrics.description: fareypoly(f, g[, m]); f poly, g poly, m int. Returns a list l where r/t (r:=l[1], t:=l[2]) is a univariate rational function such that r/t = g mod f, gcd(r,t)=gcd(f,t)=1 and deg(r) + deg(t) < deg(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Optional m controls normalization of t (m=0 leading coeff 1; m!=0 constant term normalized to 1). In positive characteristic equality mod f may fail; require deg(f) > deg(g). Examples show outputs over various rings and normalizations. Use for reconstructing rational functions modulo polynomials.

rubrics_metrics.name: polyInterpolation
rubrics_metrics.description: polyInterpolation(d, e[, n, L]); d list, e list, n int, L list. Returns list lp where f:=lp[1] is polynomial of degree <= size(d)-1 satisfying f(d[i])=e[i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies Newton interpolation in specified variable (default first). Optional n selects variable; optional L can supply existing interpolation data to add points. Elements in d must be distinct. Examples show interpolation over various rings and adding points to existing interpolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: BerlekampMassey
rubrics_metrics.description: BerlekampMassey(L, i[, M]); L list, i int, M list. Returns a list Tr where Tr[1] is the minimal polynomial (w.r.t. i-th variable) generated by the sequence L[j] if the sequence is long enough; Tr[2] is the required length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies Berlekamp–Massey to compute minimal linear recurrence; if polynomial does not factor into distinct linear factors, additional sequence elements M can be provided to extend the sequence. Examples show constructing Recurrence and checking factorization and sequence length needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: sparseInterpolation
rubrics_metrics.description: sparseInterpolation(Br, La, lpr, n[, m]); Br poly, La list, lpr list, n int, m int. Returns a polynomial B in Q[var(n+1),... ] satisfying La[i] = B(lpr[1]^i,...).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: Br is minimal polynomial from BerlekampMassey applied to La; lpr must be list of distinct primes assigned to variables. Optional m sets exponent start. Examples reconstruct sparse multivariate polynomials from evaluations using modular methods. Use for sparse interpolation from evaluation sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: ffmodStd
rubrics_metrics.description: ffmodStd(I); I ideal. Return: Groebner basis of I over an algebraic function field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show Groebner bases computed over function field parameters. See also nfmodStd. Use when computing Groebner bases where coefficients are rational functions in parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: finitediff lib issues
rubrics_metrics.description: List of outstanding issues for finitediff.lib: installation of qepcadfilter.pl needs resolution; tests for most procedures missing; global variables need cleaning; temporary files need cleaning and unique names; Top namespace pollution; poor procedure naming (e.g., 'u' is not a good name).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are project-quality and maintenance concerns that affect reliability and installation. Users should be aware of these shortcomings before deploying finitediff.lib in production.

rubrics_metrics.name: visualize
rubrics_metrics.description: visualize(f); f of type poly. Return: string that translates polynomial form of a finite-difference scheme into an indexed form (as seen in literature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: visualize converts polynomial expression into indexed U(time,space) notation. Use for presenting schemes in conventional indexed notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: u (helper for derivatives/monomials)
rubrics_metrics.description: u(D[, #]); D a string occurring in derivatives list, # an optional list of integers. Return: vector giving the vector that corresponds with gen(n)*m where m is the monomial defined by #.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: u(Ux) returns vector; u(Ux,2,3,7) returns [t^2*x^3*y^7]. Use to convert derivative name + index list into monomial/vector form used in scheme construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: scheme([v1,..,vn]); v1,..,vn of type vector. Return: poly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: performs substitutions via Groebner basis computation of the submodule generated by input vectors, then intersects intermediate result to get a finite-difference scheme. Note: works only for single PDE; for systems use matrixsystem. Example: scheme(u(Ut)+a*u(Ux), ...) yields polynomial describing scheme. Use to derive finite-difference scheme polynomial from approximations.

rubrics_metrics.name: laxfrT
rubrics_metrics.description: laxfrT(U1,U2,var); U1, U2 derivative names, var a variable in the basering. Return: vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives predefined Lax–Friedrichs approximation for time derivative (as used in literature). Warning: not interchangeable with laxfrX. Example and note: intended for time-variable discretization templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: laxfrX
rubrics_metrics.description: laxfrX(U1,U2,var); U1, U2 derivative names, var a variable in the basering. Return: vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives predefined Lax–Friedrichs approximation for a spatial derivative. Warning: not interchangeable with laxfrT. Use for spatial discretization template.

rubrics_metrics.name: forward
rubrics_metrics.description: forward(U1,U2,var); U1, U2 derivative names, var a variable in the basering. Return: vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives predefined forward approximation (common finite-difference forward difference). Examples show output vectors for forward approximations in t,x,y. Use for forward-difference discretizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: backward
rubrics_metrics.description: backward(U1,U2,var); U1, U2 derivative names, var a variable in the basering. Return: vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives predefined backward approximation. Examples show outputs. Use for backward-difference discretizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: central1st
rubrics_metrics.description: central1st(U1,U2,var); U1, U2 derivative names, var a variable in the basering. Return: vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides first-order central difference approximation vector. Use as central-difference template for first-order derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: central2nd
rubrics_metrics.description: central2nd(U1,U2,var); U1, U2 derivative names, var a variable in the basering. Return: vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides second-order central difference approximation (templates for second-order derivatives). Examples illustrate returned vector with dx^2 or dt^2 coefficients. Use for second-order discretizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: trapezoid
rubrics_metrics.description: trapezoid(U1,U2,var); U1, U2 derivative names, var a variable in the basering. Return: vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives trapezoid (Crank–Nicolson-like) approximation vector. Examples show (dx)/2*x+(dx)/2 etc. Use for mixed implicit-explicit time/spatial discretizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: midpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: midpoint(U1,U2,var); U1, U2 derivative names, var a variable in the basering. Return: vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides midpoint-approximation template. Example: midpoint(Ux,U,x) returns vector appropriate for midpoint discretization. Use as another temporal/spatial discretization option.

rubrics_metrics.name: pyramid
rubrics_metrics.description: pyramid(U1,U2,var); U1, U2 derivative names, var a variable in the basering. Return: vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a 'pyramid' approximation template frequently used in literature. Example shows polynomial coefficients like (dx)/3*x^2+(dx)/3*x+(dx)/3. Use for particular scheme shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: setinitials
rubrics_metrics.description: setinitials(V,D[,P]); V,D,P are lists of strings. Return: no return value (sets state).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: sets dependence order of derivatives, constructs suitable ring containing chosen parameters, sets new basering. P optional introduces additional symbolic parameters and symbolically introduces sine/cosine values under names like 'cx' := cos(dx*ksi), artificial parameters I,T,Px,Py introduced for eigenvalue analysis. Variables can be transformed into parameters. Use before building schemes to configure ring and parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: errormap
rubrics_metrics.description: errormap(f); f of type poly. Return: poly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performs Fourier transformation of a single polynomial (error mapping). Example: errormap converts polynomial to expression in i, sx, cx, T etc. Use to analyze Fourier symbol or dispersion/error of a scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrixsystem
rubrics_metrics.description: matrixsystem(M,A); M = list of square matrices Mt,M1,..,Mn; A = At,A1,..,An approximations. Return: matrix (or list) representing finite-difference scheme matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to solve Mt*U_t + M1*U_x1 + ... = 0 numerically by finite differences for systems of PDEs. Output: matrices B1,B2 representing scheme partitioned into time levels in form B1*U(t=N)=B2*U(t<N). Example demonstrates matrix entries. Use for systems (not single PDE).

rubrics_metrics.name: timestep
rubrics_metrics.description: timestep(M); M a square matrix with polynomials over the basering as entries. Return: list giving two matrices M1,M2 splitting M with respect to degree of the time variable t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to be used for finite-difference-scheme construction and partition into several time steps. M1 contains highest time-level polynomials and M2 lower levels. Example shows returned split matrices. Use to isolate time-level contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: fouriersystem
rubrics_metrics.description: fouriersystem(M,A); M a list of matrices, A a list of approximations. Return: list of matrices obtained by substituting approximations into PDE system, partitioning into timesteps and Fourier-transforming parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry is a matrix obtained by substitution and Fourier transform; examples show matrices with I*T*Sx+T*Cx entries etc. Use to obtain Fourier-symbol matrices of discretized PDE systems for stability/dispersion analysis.
